The visual half of `dev/plan-column-widths.md` — the tests assert the numbers,
this shows what they look like. One section per behavior, each with what to
look for. Sections accrue as the plan proceeds; nothing here is discarded, so
a later change that breaks an earlier section is visible immediately.

**Judge the PDF.** The HTML renderer emits no widths at all by design — the
browser measures — so none of this applies to it.

Render with the project venv:

```powershell
$env:QUARTO_PYTHON = "$PWD/.venv/Scripts/python.exe"
quarto render dev/check-widths.qmd --to pdf
```

Note the preamble loads `newtxtext`. The width estimator is Times metrics, so
it is exact against newtx (what `Etcher` uses) and about 11% tight against
Latin Modern, the LaTeX default a plain Quarto PDF would use. Drop that line
and section 1's headings start hyphenating — which is itself worth seeing
once. Use `newtxtext` alone: `newtxmath` collides with Quarto's math setup
(`\arrowvert already defined`).

```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd
from greater_tables import GT, Fabricator, __version__
print(f'greater_tables {__version__}')
```

## 1. A long heading no longer stretches its column

Before: the column was as wide as `Cumulative Incurred Loss` set on one line
(about 12em). Now the heading wraps and the column is as wide as its widest
word, `Cumulative` (about 5.4em).

**Look for:** three narrow columns of numbers with wrapped headings above
them — not three very wide columns with one-line headings.

```{python}
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Cumulative Incurred Loss': [1234.5, 2345.6, 3456.7],
    'Cumulative Paid Loss': [1000.0, 2000.0, 3000.0],
    'Case Outstanding Reserve': [234.5, 345.6, 456.7],
}, index=pd.Index([2022, 2023, 2024], name='Accident Year'))
GT(df, caption='Long headings over narrow numeric columns')
```

## 2. Cells that fit no longer wrap anyway

The bug: a column set to exactly its content's natural width still broke the
line, because TikZ's `align=left` is *balanced* ragged. `Sub 1` came out as
`Sub` over `1`. Now `align=flush left`.

**Look for:** `Sub 1` and `Sub 2` each on **one line** in the stub.

```{python}
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Paid': [1234.5, float('nan'), 1234.5],
    'Incurred': [-89.0, 12.3, -76.7],
}, index=pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples(
    [(2020, 'Sub 1'), (2020, 'Sub 2'), ('Total', '')],
    names=['Year', 'Sub']))
GT(df, caption='Stub values that exactly fit their column')
```

## 3. Glyph widths: em dash, percent, micro, hyphen

`—` was estimated at 0.6em against a true 1.0em, `%` at 0.6 against 0.833,
`µ` at 0.6 against 0.5, and `-` at 0.5 against 0.333. So missing-value
columns and ratio columns were under-reserved (text crowding the neighbor)
and date columns over-reserved (a visible gap).

**Look for:** the `—` markers sitting clear of the next column; percentages
not touching their neighbor; dates with no odd trailing gap.

```{python}
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'loss ratio': [0.458, 0.612, float('nan'), 0.397],
    'missing': [float('nan'), 1.5, float('nan'), 2.5],
    'as of': pd.to_datetime(['2024-01-15', '2024-06-30',
                             '2025-01-15', '2025-06-30']),
    'tiny': [1.2e-6, 3.4e-6, 5.6e-6, 7.8e-6],
}, index=['alpha', 'beta', 'gamma', 'delta'])
GT(df, ratio_cols=['loss ratio'], caption='Em dash, percent, SI micro, dates')
```

## 4. Spanning labels are measured at all

A group label sits as an overlaid node with no text width, so it cannot wrap.
Previously it contributed nothing to the width calculation and simply
overflowed its group; now it widens the last column it covers.

**Look for:** the long group label fitting inside its two columns, not
spilling over the rules on either side.

```{python}
df = Fabricator(seed=42).make(6, 'ff', column_groups=2)
df.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples([
    ('A Notably Long Group Label', 'paid'),
    ('A Notably Long Group Label', 'incurred'),
    ('Short', 'paid'),
    ('Short', 'incurred'),
][:len(df.columns)])
GT(df, caption='A group label wider than the columns beneath it')
```

## 5. Prose wraps at the per-column cap (regression check)

Unchanged behavior, kept so you can confirm nothing regressed: a wrapping
column stops at `HouseStyle.max_prose_width_em` (18em) however long its cells
are, and numeric columns never wrap.

```{python}
df = Fabricator(seed=115).make(5, 'w10w4f',
                               metric_name_spec=['variable length text',
                                                 'short variable', 'amount'])
GT(df, caption='Long prose beside numeric columns')
```

## 6. A width budget narrows prose, in step

`max_table_width_em` is a target for the whole table. Prose columns give way
first, all together — one shared quantile, so no column is singled out — and
numbers, dates and headers never move. Same table three times.

**Look for:** the text columns getting narrower and taller down the page while
the `amount` column stays put and the table's right edge marches left.

```{python}
#| output: asis
from greater_tables import HouseStyle, build, TableSpec, render_tikz
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

wide = Fabricator(seed=115).make(4, 'w10w4f',
                                 metric_name_spec=['variable length text',
                                                   'short variable', 'amount'])
doc = build(wide, TableSpec())
for budget in (None, 38, 28):
    label = 'no budget' if budget is None else f'max_table_width_em={budget}'
    display(Markdown(f'**{label}**\n'))
    print(render_tikz(doc, HouseStyle(max_table_width_em=budget,
                                      tikz_container_env='figure')))
```

## 7. A table of numbers has nothing to give, so it scales

Every column here is unbreakable, so no allocation can help. The budget then
steps `tikz_scale` down a coarse ladder and logs what it did — advisory, as
documented, never silent.

**Look for:** the second table visibly smaller in font as well as narrower,
rather than columns being squeezed.

```{python}
#| output: asis
numbers = Fabricator(seed=105).make(8, 'fi', index_levels=2, column_groups=2)
ndoc = build(numbers, TableSpec())
for budget in (None, 22):
    label = 'no budget' if budget is None else f'max_table_width_em={budget}'
    display(Markdown(f'**{label}**\n'))
    print(render_tikz(ndoc, HouseStyle(max_table_width_em=budget,
                                       tikz_container_env='figure')))
```

## 8. The same budget in HTML

Render this document `--to html` and the tables above carry
`--gt-max-width` / `--gt-prose-max` on the wrapper. No solver runs there: the
`gt-nowrap` class already pins the columns that must not be narrowed, so the
browser narrows exactly the prose ones using real font metrics rather than
our estimate.
